title: How to further protect victims' rights: Submit ideas by 5 November
content: The European Commission launched an open public consultation to gather feedback for its new EU Strategy on victims’ rights. Victims of crime, citizens as well as all relevant actors in the field are invited to contribute. You can submit your contribution until 5 November 2026.

title: How EU research can help respond to heatwaves
content: With climate change, Europe is getting warmer and heatwaves are becoming more frequent and intense. While the immediate focus is on responding to the emergencies, EU-funded research develops the knowledge and solutions needed to strengthen society’s resilience.

title: EU launches AI Gigafactories call
content: The EU has launched a call for tenders to establish up to seven AI Gigafactories across Europe. The initiative will expand Europe's AI computing capacity and give all relevant actors access to infrastructure for training, inference and fine-tuning advanced frontier AI models.

content: The European Commission is preparing a new set of policy initiatives on school education. Citizens and stakeholders are invited to share their views on the Commission’s planned actions in key areas: basic skills, attractiveness of the teaching profession, and digital education infrastructure.

title: Right to repair: New consumer rights for easy and attractive repairs
content: The Directive on repair of goods became national law across EU countries on 31 July 2026. The new rules will help create a system that favours repairing a product over purchasing a new one. They will help consumers save, boost the circular economy and support sustainable consumption.

title: Know your EU passenger rights before you travel
content: If you’re heading off on a summer break soon, rest assured that the EU has you covered if your travel plans run into trouble. Whether your flight is cancelled, your train delayed or your luggage lost aboard your cruise ship, you have the right to make a claim under EU-wide passenger rights.

title: Frontex co-led operation seizes nearly half a tonne of cocaine off European shores
content: Nearly half a tonne of cocaine, dropped in open water for small boats to scoop up before it reached European shores, has been seized in a sea operation co-led by Frontex. Some 14 countries spent a month targeting drug traffickers at sea before seizing the 454 kg of cocaine and arresting 5 suspects.

title: Cast your vote on new euro banknote design proposals
content: Have your say on the ten shortlisted design proposals for the next series of euro banknotes that have been unveiled by the European Central Bank. An online survey where you can give your feedback is open until 21 September. The winning proposal will be selected around the end of the year.

title: New EU energy rules: cleaner, more secure energy and stronger consumer protection
content: New electricity and gas market rules are taking effect across the EU. They aim to make Europe’s energy system cleaner, more secure and resilient. They protect citizens from energy price spikes and give them stronger rights and control over their energy choices.

title: Google fined for breaching Digital Markets Act
content: The Commission found that Google had breached the DMA by favouring its own services in Google Search and by imposing restrictions preventing businesses from directing consumers to alternative, often lower-cost, purchasing channels on Google Play. The Commission imposed total fines of €890 million.

title: A renewed commitment to protect and empower the EU's citizens
content: The European Pillar of Social Rights helps to improve people's lives through better jobs, equal opportunities, quality working conditions and strong social protection. A communication has been published that looks at its impact and highlights three areas which require urgent additional attention.

title: A plan to make Europe the first electro-continent
content: The Commission has put forward the electrification action plan as part of the EU’s wider efforts to boost Europe’s competitiveness, decarbonisation and independence. The plan introduces measures to make electricity more competitive and to incentivise the use of electricity-based technologies.

title: Rule of law report strengthens EU democracy and fundamental rights
content: The 2026 Rule of Law report shows how well the rule of law is holding up across the EU and 4 potential EU members: Albania, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. It finds that, while some challenges persist, there is continued progress in many EU countries, with many reforms completed or underway.

title: Europeans call for stronger action on children's online safety, survey finds
content: A new survey shows that Europeans are overwhelmingly concerned about all the risks children face on social media. Cyberbullying and harassment top the list of concerns, worrying 71% of respondents. Europeans also call for more democratic participation, defence capabilities and renewable energy.
snippet: A new survey shows that Europeans are overwhelmingly concerned about all the risks children face on social media. Cyberbullying and harassment top the list of concerns, worrying 71% of respondents.

title: New EU measures support European farmers facing high fertiliser costs
content: New EU measures will help farmers address the sharp increase in fertiliser and other input costs triggered by the recent crisis in the Middle East. They will allow EU countries to provide urgent and targeted financial support to farmers facing rising production costs and liquidity pressures.

title: Safer cars, safer roads: New rules take effect
content: Starting on 7 July 2026, all newly registered cars and vans in the EU will be subject to more advanced safety requirements. This is the latest phase in the rollout of EU vehicle safety rules under the General Safety Regulation, and will contribute to making Europe's roads safer.

title: New EU plan to address the risks and opportunities of advanced AI for cybersecurity
content: The European Commission has presented a plan to address the risks and harness the opportunities of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) in cybersecurity. It builds on existing EU rules and aims to strengthen the EU’s cybersecurity framework.

title: New plan to boost resilience and prosperity of livestock farming
content: A new EU strategy for the livestock sector sets out actions to help farmers address current economic, environmental and market challenges. Based on five priority areas, including sustainability and competitiveness, the strategy aims to make the livestock sector more prosperous and resilient overall.

title: Clearer social benefits rules for EU mobile workers
content: Updated EU social benefits rules ensure fair and clear access to social security for EU workers who live or work in another EU country. They update criteria on receiving unemployment, family and long-term care benefits and encourage EU countries to share information to help root out benefits fraud.

title: Use of plastic packaging material on the rise in the EU
content: A new EU study has found that plastic is the only packaging material that is on the rise, growing by 11 percent between 2011 and 2025. The study looked at the use of all packaging materials including plastic, glass, paper and metals in 19 EU countries during this period.

title: International Plastic Bag Free Day – from single use to reuse
content: To raise awareness about eliminating plastic bag use worldwide and promote eco-friendly reusable alternatives, we observe International Plastic Bag Free Day every 3 July. On this occasion, take a look at how EU rules are helping to drastically reduce the consumption and use of plastics.

title: €2.5 billion of EU Emissions Trading System revenues invested in cleaner energy systems
content: Over 50 energy-related projects in the EU will receive €2.5 billion from an EU fund financed by revenues from the EU Emissions Trading System. The projects focus on renewable electricity generation, the modernisation of energy networks and energy efficiency.

title: Ireland takes over Council presidency
content: On 1 July 2026, Ireland took over the Presidency of the Council of the European Union. It will steer the work of the Council for the next six months. Learn more about its priorities and activities.
